headline: EEG decoding is tested for transfer across subjects, stimuli and deployment, with controls exposing spurious accuracy
label: Neural Decoding Validity
summary: New preprints stress cross-subject transfer, adaptation cost and sham controls, showing decoding accuracy may not hold beyond the conditions where it was measured.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether EEG and neural decoding performance holds outside the conditions in which it was measured. ReBrain transfers an intracranial EEG prior to scalp signals without paired data or fine-tuning, and AMRT reports cross-subject generalization for continuous motor decoding. The BCI study frames adapting frozen EEG encoders as a resource-priced decision using gated Bayesian heads. The EEG-video study is most explicit on validity: contrastive alignment beats CCA for seen stimuli but not novel videos, and a sham control shows accuracy can be spurious. NeuroSim adds a simulator with injected disease biomarkers for classifier development. What is new is the emphasis on transfer, adaptation cost and negative controls. None of the items tests a causal or mechanistic account, so mechanistic validity remains open.
